titulo: Inside Google (2/3): chips, Nobels, robotaxis & quantum 🧬 #shorts
descripcion:
Inside the Magnificent 7 · Google, part 2 of 3: what it's researching.

🧬 DeepMind: AlphaFold, 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (Hassabis & Jumper) · Gemini app at 1B users
🔧 TPUs: 8th generation (TPU 8t for training, TPU 8i for inference), April 2026; also sold to other companies
⚛️ Willow: a sub-5-minute calculation that would take a supercomputer 10^25 years (Dec 2024) · Michel Devoret, 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics
🚕 Waymo: ~500,000 paid rides/week in 10 cities (March 2026), goal of 1M by year end
💸 Other Bets: $2.04B loss in Jul–Sep 2026

escenas.texto: Google isn't just a search engine. Part two of three: its four big bets on the future.
Bet one: DeepMind, its A I lab. It built AlphaFold, which predicts the shape of proteins, and that's why Demis Hassabis and John Jumper won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in twenty twenty four.
DeepMind also makes Gemini. Its app now has one billion users, and it's the fastest growing product in Google's history.

Bet two: its own chips, called TPUs. In April it unveiled the eighth generation, split in two: one chip to train models and one to run them. And it now sells them to other companies, including Anthropic, the maker of Claude.
Bet three: quantum computing. Its Willow chip did a calculation in under five minutes that would take a supercomputer ten septillion years.
And its chief scientist for quantum hardware, Michel Devoret, won the Nobel Prize in Physics in twenty twenty five.

visual.sub: in Physics, for its hardware chief scientist

escenas.texto: Bet four: Waymo, driverless taxis. By March it was giving half a million paid rides a week in ten U S cities, and its goal is one million before the year ends.
And what does all this cost? The other bets, including Waymo, lost two point zero four billion dollars this quarter alone.
In part three: is Google winning the A I race? And is its stock cheap or expensive? Subscribe.
